tools.name: listDeployments
tools.description: Returns all Cube deployments and their agents that you can access. Use this to discover valid deploymentId values before passing them to any other tool: every tool takes an optional deploymentId and defaults to the deployment this session connected to, so pass one explicitly whenever the user asks about a different deployment. Passing an id not listed here is rejected. Every deployment supports the Auto agent (pass agentId: null to chat) — the default agent used when no specific agent is selected — in addition to any configured agents listed.

tools.name: searchDataModel
tools.description: Search the Cube semantic model by similarity — views and their measures & dimensions — to discover what is queryable. Returns compact records (name, title, description, type) you can then reference in a runQuery SQL statement. Call this before runQuery to find the exact view and member names, and pass the same `branchName` to both so the members you find are the ones the query will see: on a dev branch this reports THAT branch’s un-deployed model, including members that do not exist in production yet. The model searched is reported back as `branchName` (null = deployed model).

branchName.description: Dev branch to run this call against, as returned by startDataModelEdit. The call then runs on that branch’s dev worker — its un-deployed data model, including members that exist only there, and its own agent configuration (skills, rules, spaces) — which is how a branch is verified before it is deployed. Only dev branches (`dev-<user>-<hash>`) run a worker that can serve a request; any other branch is rejected rather than silently answered from production. Omit to use the branch this session is connected to (the deployed model, unless the endpoint named one); pass null to force the deployed model. The branch actually used is reported back as `branchName` (null = deployed model).

deploymentId.description: Deployment to run this call against. Defaults to the deployment this session is connected to. Call listDeployments to discover valid ids — passing one you were not offered is rejected.

limit.description: Max number of views to return (default 50).

query.description: Optional natural-language query, matched by semantic similarity against views and their members (names, titles, descriptions, and AI context) — so it finds relevant concepts even without a literal keyword overlap. Prefer a short descriptive phrase over single keywords — e.g. "monthly revenue", "customer churn", "proof of concept deals". Omit to list the whole model.

tools.name: runQuery
tools.description: Run a Cube SQL query against the Cube SQL API (PostgreSQL dialect — see https://docs.cube.dev/reference/core-data-apis/sql-api) and return the result rows. Returns `schema` (columns), a page of `data` rows (page size 100), and `hasMore`/`totalRows` for pagination via `offset`. Read-only — it does not modify the model, workbooks, or reports. Use searchDataModel first to find the exact cubes/views and members to query — never guess member names, and call it with the same `branchName` so it reports the same model this query will run against. Pass `branchName` to run against a dev branch's un-deployed model instead of the deployed one; the branch the query actually ran on comes back as `branchName` (null = deployed model). ## CubeSQL Query Rules - When querying measures, always use MEASURE() function, e.g. MEASURE(revenue), do not nest MEASURE() in other functions. SUM(MEASURE(revenue)) IS INVALID and NOT ALLOWED, use MEASURE(revenue) instead. - A condition that narrows the WHOLE result ("only completed orders", "just the US") is a WHERE clause on the query, and every measure stays MEASURE(): SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at), MEASURE(revenue) FROM orders_view WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY 1.

branchName.description: Dev branch to run this call against, as returned by startDataModelEdit. Only dev branches (`dev-<user>-<hash>`) run a worker that can serve a request; any other branch is rejected rather than silently answered from production. Omit to use the branch this session is connected to (the deployed model, unless the endpoint named one); pass null to force the deployed model. The branch actually used is reported back as `branchName` (null = deployed model).

deploymentId.description: Deployment to run this call against. Defaults to the deployment this session is connected to. Call listDeployments to discover valid ids — passing one you were not offered is rejected.

offset.description: Zero-based row offset of the page to return. Page size is fixed at 100; paginate by incrementing offset until hasMore is false.

sqlQuery.description: A Cube SQL query (PostgreSQL dialect) against the semantic layer — e.g. `SELECT status, MEASURE(count) FROM orders GROUP BY 1`. Use searchDataModel first to find the cubes/views and members to query.

timezone.description: IANA time zone to run the query in, e.g. `America/New_York`. Omit to use the deployment default (UTC unless configured).

tools.name: chat
tools.description: Ask a question about your data through the Cube semantic layer. The agent queries the existing semantic model, runs SQL against your governed metrics and dimensions, and searches existing reports to ground its answers. This tool is read-only — it does not modify the data model, files, workbooks, or reports. If the user asks for a chart, graph, table, visualization, or dashboard-style output, answer in text because the visualize tool is not available for this client. Pass `branchName` to run the turn against a dev branch's un-deployed data model AND its agent configuration (skills, rules, spaces), which is how a branch is exercised before it is deployed; the branch used comes back as `branchName` (null = deployed model). A conversation stays on the branch it started on, so omit `branchName` when resuming with a `chatId` and start a new chat to ask the same question of another branch. The response's `cubeChatUrl` field is the only valid link to this conversation in Cube — no other URL opens it. It is null when the conversation has no linkable Cube page.

agentId.description: Agent ID to use for this request. When omitted or null, the deployment default (Auto) agent is used. Must belong to the target deployment.

Only dev branches (`dev-<user>-<hash>`) run a worker that can serve a request; any other branch is rejected rather than silently answered from production. Omit to use the branch this session is connected to (the deployed model, unless the endpoint named one); pass null to force the deployed model. The branch actually used is reported back as `branchName` (null = deployed model).

deploymentId.description: Deployment to run this call against. Defaults to the deployment this session is connected to. Call listDeployments to discover valid ids — passing one you were not offered is rejected.

tools.name: listDataModelFiles
tools.description: List the Cube semantic model SOURCE files (the raw `.yml` / `.js` / `.py` schema files that define cubes and views) on a branch. Use this to discover which files to read/edit — it complements searchDataModel, which returns the compiled meta rather than the editable source. Data-model editing workflow (edit the Cube semantic model / schema YAML on a dev branch, never production): startDataModelEdit (enter dev mode → dev branchName) → readDataModelFile / writeDataModelFile / deleteDataModelFile (pass that branchName) → getDataModelChanges (review the diff) → runQuery with that same branchName (verify the edited model returns the right rows before deploying). Use listDataModelFiles / readDataModelFile to discover the current model source, getBranchDiff to see what ANY branch changed relative to the deploy branch, and getDeploymentEnv to check the deployment’s configuration. Call getBranchState whenever you need to know which branch you and the USER are each on. Your edits stay invisible — to the user, to the Cube UI and to anyone reviewing — until commitDataModelChanges commits the dev branch onto its parent; then offer switchUserBranch so the user is looking at that branch, commitToNewBranch to put the work on a branch of its own, discardDataModelChanges to start over, and mergeToDefaultBranch (only when the user asks to publish) to make it live.

branchName.description: Branch to read from. Omit to use the branch this session is connected to (the deploy branch, unless the endpoint named one); pass null to force the deploy branch.

deploymentId.description: Deployment to run this call against. Defaults to the deployment this session is connected to. Call listDeployments to discover valid ids — passing one you were not offered is rejected.

Editing always happens on this dev branch — the deploy branch is never writable. Call this first, before any edit. To RESUME a specific edit later, pass the same feature-branch name you used before; omitting `branchName` starts a NEW edit session each call, so reuse the returned branchName for all follow-up tools rather than calling this again. Data-model editing workflow (edit the Cube semantic model / schema YAML on a dev branch, never production): startDataModelEdit (enter dev mode → dev branchName) → readDataModelFile / writeDataModelFile / deleteDataModelFile (pass that branchName) → getDataModelChanges (review the diff) → runQuery with that same branchName (verify the edited model returns the right rows before deploying). branchName.description: Optional label for the feature branch this edit lives on (e.g. `add-revenue-measure`); it becomes the dev branch’s parent. Auto-generated when omitted. The editable dev branch is derived from it and returned as `branchName` in the result.

tools.name: commitDataModelChanges
tools.description: Commit the dev branch’s edits onto the branch it was created from. This is what makes your work exist outside the development session: until you call it, everything writeDataModelFile saved lives only in the dev worker’s working copy — it is not on any branch the user can select, nobody reviewing sees it, and telling the user the change is ready would be wrong. Call it once the model compiles; the dev branch stays usable afterwards so you can keep editing. Usually the parent is an ordinary branch and this does NOT touch production — but a dev branch created from the deployment’s default branch publishes live, and that call is refused until the user has confirmed it. Afterwards, name the branch it reports (`targetBranchName`) to the user and offer switchUserBranch so they can look at it. Data-model editing workflow (edit the Cube semantic model / schema YAML on a dev branch, never production): startDataModelEdit (enter dev mode → dev branchName) → readDataModelFile / writeDataModelFile / deleteDataModelFile (pass that branchName) → getDataModelChanges (review the diff) → runQuery with that same branchName (verify the edited model returns the right rows before deploying). Use listDataModelFiles / readDataModelFile to discover the current model source, getBranchDiff to see what ANY branch changed relative to the deploy branch, and getDeploymentEnv to check the deployment’s configuration. Call getBranchState whenever you need to know which branch you and the USER are each on. Your edits stay invisible — to the user, to the Cube UI and to anyone reviewing — until commitDataModelChanges commits the dev branch onto its parent; then offer switchUserBranch so the user is looking at that branch, commitToNewBranch to put the work on a branch of its own, discardDataModelChanges to start over, and mergeToDefaultBranch (only when the user asks to publish) to make it live.

Set it only after the user has explicitly confirmed they want that, never to retry a refusal on your own.

tools.name: mergeToDefaultBranch

This is a publish step with real consequences, so call it ONLY when the user has explicitly asked to publish or merge to production — never on your own initiative after committing. Commit first with commitDataModelChanges: this merges committed branches, not the development session. Prefer letting the user test the branch first (switchUserBranch). tools.name: createWorkbook
tools.description: Create a new empty workbook — the container that holds reports and a dashboard. Returns its numeric `workbookId` (which every other dashboard tool needs) and a `url` you can share with the user to open the new dashboard. Do NOT create a workbook if you were given one to build into. Dashboard-authoring workflow (use together): createWorkbook → createReport (one per chart/visualization) → updateDashboard → publishDashboard; readWorkbook reads the current state. To manage an EXISTING report (standalone or workbook-bound) rather than recreating it: readReport, updateReport (edit its title / SQL / visualization / placement in place, keeping its reportId), deleteReport.

deploymentId.description: Deployment to run this call against. Defaults to the deployment this session is connected to. Call listDeployments to discover valid ids — passing one you were not offered is rejected.

description.description: Optional description shown to viewers. Stored on the workbook.

name.description: Name of the workbook (also the dashboard title).

tools.name: createReport
tools.description: Save a query + its visualization as a Report, and return its numeric `reportId` and a `url`. The report always carries a chartCategory: "table" (default), "vega" (pass vegaSpec for a Vega-Lite graph), "kpi" (pass kpiChartSpec for a KPI metric tile), "html" (pass htmlChartSpec), "map" (pass mapChartSpec), or "sankey" (pass sankeyChartSpec for a flow diagram). WHERE IT LANDS is decided by `workbookId`: WITH a workbookId the report becomes a tab of that workbook and can be referenced by a CHART widget on that workbook's dashboard — create it here first, then pass the returned `reportId` to updateDashboard. WITHOUT a workbookId it is a standalone exploration at the workspace root (or under `folderId`), which no dashboard widget can reference. Never invent a reportId. Dashboard-authoring workflow (use together): createWorkbook → createReport (one per chart/visualization) → updateDashboard → publishDashboard; readWorkbook reads the current state. To manage an EXISTING report (standalone or workbook-bound) rather than recreating it: readReport, updateReport (edit its title / SQL / visualization / placement in place, keeping its reportId), deleteReport.

folderId.description: Optional workspace folder for a standalone report (ignored when workbookId is set).

title.description: Report title shown on the chart tile.

vegaSpec.description: Vega-Lite v5 chart spec — REQUIRED when chartCategory is "vega". Its field names must match the SQL result columns; always provide empty data with 'table' name so it can be inlined later. (Abridged in this eval fixture.)

Dashboard-authoring workflow (use together): createWorkbook → createReport (one per chart/visualization) → updateDashboard → publishDashboard; readWorkbook reads the current state. tools.name: updateDashboard
tools.description: Save the dashboard layout (the full `widgets` array) to the workbook DRAFT. This does not go live until publishDashboard. Send the COMPLETE widget set every time. CHART widgets must reference a real reportId from a createReport call made WITH this same workbookId. Grid rules: 12 columns (x + w ≤ 12); CHART h≈11. Pass `oldDashboardConfig` (from readWorkbook) for a safe concurrent update. Returns a `url` to the updated dashboard. Dashboard-authoring workflow (use together): createWorkbook → createReport (one per chart/visualization) → updateDashboard → publishDashboard; readWorkbook reads the current state. To manage an EXISTING report (standalone or workbook-bound) rather than recreating it: readReport, updateReport (edit its title / SQL / visualization / placement in place, keeping its reportId), deleteReport.

tools.name: publishDashboard

Dashboard-authoring workflow (use together): createWorkbook → createReport (one per chart/visualization) → updateDashboard → publishDashboard; readWorkbook reads the current state. To manage an EXISTING report (standalone or workbook-bound) rather than recreating it: readReport, updateReport (edit its title / SQL / visualization / placement in place, keeping its reportId), deleteReport.
